title: Separately adopted fixed-background Maxwell and charged probes

items.title: Separately adopted fixed-background Maxwell and charged probes
items.physical_scope: A separately adopted classical test model on a prescribed smooth Lorentzian metric: smooth source-free or prescribed-source Maxwell fields and massive charged probes on finite local-potential worldline segments. The metric and field are fixed inputs; no Einstein equation is imposed on them, no probe self-field or self-gravity is evaluated, and no small-backreaction limit, global potential, global trajectory, or empirical validity is asserted. Geometric-optics use is limited to the exact finite-order phase, amplitude, constraint, and compact-region bounds in the listed mathematical supplier.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, state the prescribed charged-particle Lorentz equation in curved spacetime; equations (6.12)–(6.14), PDF pp. 63–64, derive null geometric-optics rays. Source normalization is not imported.

references.title: Eric Poisson, Adam Pound and Ian Vega, The Motion of Point Particles in Curved Spacetime, author manuscript arXiv:1102.0529v3 (2011), complete 162-page review
references.locator: §18.1, equations (18.3)–(18.10), PDF pp. 96–98, gives the proper-time action, Maxwell source and Lorentz-force equation for a point electric charge; the authors explicitly state that its self-field is singular on the worldline and the equation is only formal until that issue is treated. This item adopts an external smooth field and does not import a self-force result.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes (2019)
references.locator: §1.2.3, equation (1.20), PDF pp. 23–24, presents the charged-particle action in an electromagnetic potential; §1.2.4, PDF pp. 25–26, places test-particle motion in a curved metric. The notes use their own units and signs; the present action and local SI conventions are those of the exact listed suppliers.

references.title: A. I. Harte, Gravitational lensing beyond geometric optics: I. Formalism and observables, arXiv:1808.06203v2 (2018), complete 38-page article
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 10–13, and Appendix A, PDF pp. 33–34, discuss the curved-background Maxwell potential ansatz, transport and gauge constraints, polarization, and the gauge-gradient residual after truncation. This item adopts only the finite-order scope stated by its mathematical supplier.

items.title: Controlled test-wave rays, polarization and Maxwell residual
items.physical_scope: C4 real phase and C3 complex amplitudes under the exact four finite-order constraints; finite compact-chart component residual and leading-field bounds only; local affine null rays and the two-dimensional transverse polarization quotient. The construction is interpreted as a fixed-background Maxwell test field and gives no convergence, global caustic control, exact-solution error, Einstein equation, or backreaction estimate.

references.title: A. I. Harte, Gravitational lensing beyond geometric optics: I. Formalism and observables, arXiv:1808.06203v2 (2018), complete 38-page article
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, equations (40)–(55), PDF pp. 10–13, treat the curved Maxwell potential ansatz, transport/gauge constraints, leading field and polarization; Appendix A, equations (A.2)–(A.5), PDF pp. 33–34, identifies the gauge-gradient residual. The exact finite-ε identities and bounds are proved by the listed mathematical supplier.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.12)–(6.14), PDF pp. 63–64, derive null geometric-optics rays in curved spacetime. Reall's leading-order discussion does not supply the finite-ε residual bound used here.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes (2019)
references.locator: §§2.4.2 and 4.5, PDF pp. 105–109 and 190–204, give the differential-form Maxwell field and curved-spacetime field equations/stress context. The local finite-order field calculation follows the exact mathematical supplier and local SI conventions.

items.title: Exact source/test-field/backreaction consistency distinction
items.physical_scope: Fixed smooth metric with a smooth Maxwell field and explicitly stated source/dust scaling, including the exact quadratic stress residual and finite Coulomb-annulus energy calculation. This distinguishes test-field bookkeeping from a coupled solution; it constructs no nearby coupled family, singular point charge, or self-field.

references.title: Eric Poisson, Adam Pound and Ian Vega, The Motion of Point Particles in Curved Spacetime, author manuscript arXiv:1102.0529v3 (2011), complete 162-page review
references.locator: §18.1, equations (18.3)–(18.10), PDF pp. 96–98, sets out the coupled point-charge source and the formal self-field difficulty; no point-source limit is inferred here.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page notes
references.locator: §§4.3–4.5, PDF pp. 120–125, treats the Maxwell stress tensor and its observer energy in the source's Gaussian conventions; local SI stress and residual identities are those of the exact mathematical supplier.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes (2019)
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–194, treats Maxwell and matter stress tensors in curved spacetime. Its conventions are contextual; the quadratic scaling and compact-region residual are proved by the exact mathematical supplier.

items.title: Finite-time weak/slow charged probe correspondence
items.physical_scope: Finite-time comparison for a massive charged test probe on a stationary weak metric with the exact C2 remainder bounds and prescribed electric/magnetic scalings of the mathematical supplier. It requires alpha nonzero, uniformly small speed, existing trajectories, common compact containment and finite scaled duration. It solves neither Maxwell nor Einstein equations and constructs no fully coupled background family.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, give the curved-background Lorentz equation; equations (6.12)–(6.14), PDF pp. 63–64, give the leading null-ray calculation. The finite weak/slow trajectory bound follows from the exact mathematical supplier, not from this source's leading-order discussion.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §4.1, equations (4.8)–(4.21), PDF pp. 112–114, derives the static weak-field slow-motion geodesic term from the metric. The charged force and its uniform error estimate are supplied by the exact items, not inferred from Carroll's neutral-particle limit.

references.title: Eric Poisson, Adam Pound and Ian Vega, The Motion of Point Particles in Curved Spacetime, author manuscript arXiv:1102.0529v3 (2011), complete 162-page review
references.locator: §18.1, equations (18.3)–(18.10), PDF pp. 96–98, gives the curved test-particle Lorentz equation and warns that the particle's own point-charge field is singular. The present result assumes only a separately prescribed smooth external field.

title: Separately adopted fixed-background Maxwell and charged probes — Examples

items.title: Electrostatic test-energy first integral
items.physical_scope: A finite-segment charged test probe in a prescribed, stationary electrostatic potential on Minkowski spacetime. The conserved energy is conditional on the adopted Lorentz-force law and excludes self-field, self-gravity, radiation reaction, and any coupled source claim.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, state the charged test-particle Lorentz law in curved spacetime. The stationary potential and energy integral are computed here under the local model conventions.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes (2019)
references.locator: §1.2.3, equation (1.20), PDF pp. 23–24, gives the charged-particle potential action and its electrostatic potential term. The item uses the local SI action sign and proves its conservation directly.

items.title: Exact finite-frequency transverse Maxwell wave
items.physical_scope: An exact real, source-free plane-wave solution of the prescribed Minkowski Maxwell test model at every stated positive epsilon, with transverse electric/magnetic components. Its nonzero stress prevents it from solving the source-free coupled Einstein–Maxwell equation with Lambda=0 on the unchanged Minkowski metric. This is an ideal solution, not an experiment or photon-energy claim.

references.title: A. I. Harte, Gravitational lensing beyond geometric optics: I. Formalism and observables, arXiv:1808.06203v2 (2018), complete 38-page article
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 10–13, discusses transverse leading electromagnetic fields and polarization; Appendix A, PDF pp. 33–34, treats finite truncation residuals. This constant-amplitude plane wave is checked exactly here.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.12)–(6.14), PDF pp. 63–64, give the null geometric-optics ray calculation. The finite-frequency field equations and coupled-solution distinction are verified locally using the listed item suppliers.

items.title: Constant-magnetic-field slow test-orbit comparison
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-time comparison of a relativistic charged test orbit and its Newton–Lorentz slow-motion trajectory in a prescribed constant magnetic field on Minkowski space. It excludes self-field, radiation reaction, and any small-field backreaction theorem or fully coupled flat Einstein–Maxwell solution.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, give the curved charged test-particle equation; the finite magnetic orbit and error bound are computed here.
